body.para: Purpose
Creates an index (a tag in a compound index file, or a stand-alone index file), using the syntax of the FoxPro dialect. This is the FoxPro version of the INDEX command.
Syntax

INDEX ON <KeyExpression> [TAG <OrderName>] [TO | OF <IndexFile>]
[FOR <lCondition>] [WHILE <lCondition>] [<Scope>]
[UNIQUE | CANDIDATE] [ASCENDING | DESCENDING] [COMPACT] [BINARY <n>] [COLLATE <cCollation>]
[USECURRENT] [ADDITIVE] [CUSTOM] [NOOPTIMIZE]
Arguments
ON <KeyExpression>The expression that defines the index key.
TAG <OrderName>The name of the tag (order) to create.
TO | OF <IndexFile>The name of the index file. TO creates a stand-alone index file when no TAG is specified. OF creates the tag in the specified compound index file.
UNIQUEOnly the first record with a particular key value is included in the index.
CANDIDATECreates a candidate index: the key values must be unique.
ASCENDING | DESCENDINGThe order of the index. The default is ascending.
COMPACTCreates a compact index file.
BINARY <n>Creates the index with binary (ordinal) comparison of the key values.
COLLATE <cCollation>The collation sequence that is used for character keys.
USECURRENTUse the current order to limit the records that are put in the new index.
ADDITIVEKeeps the other open index files open when the new index is created.
CUSTOMCreates a custom (user maintained) index.
NOOPTIMIZEDisables the optimization of the FOR clause.
Remarks
In the FoxPro dialect the order name is specified with the TAG keyword and the index file with TO or OF. The command is translated to calls to OrdCondSet() and OrdCreate().
Examples

USE Customers EXCLUSIVE
INDEX ON UPPER(LastName) TAG LastName
INDEX ON Id TAG Id CANDIDATE
INDEX ON Country + City TAG CountryCity FOR !DELETED()
See Also
INDEX, SET INDEX (FoxPro), SET ORDER, REINDEX, OrdCondSet(), OrdCreate()
